activities.anchor: Start at the beginning of world literature
activities.caption: rebuild the first plot literature ever told
activities.name: epicGilgameshOrder

items: The gods make the wild man Enkidu to balance him
Gilgamesh crosses the waters of death to find Utnapishtim, survivor of the great flood
The test — stay awake for a week — fails in hours, asleep; the plant of youth is eaten by a serpent, and the king returns empty-handed to write the walls
config.why: Immortality is transmitted by civilisation and story, not by the body — the thesis of literature itself, stated in its first surviving masterpiece.

activities.anchor: he famously jumped up and paced
activities.caption: true or false — the flood tablet
activities.name: epicFloodJudge

statements.s: Tablet XI's flood narrative predates the earliest biblical texts by roughly a millennium.
statements.why: The arrow of time points from Gilgamesh toward Genesis — a shared ancient Near Eastern tradition, not plagiarism in either direction.

statements.s: George Smith's 1872 translation of the flood tablet caused a sensation.
statements.why: A man warned by a god, a boat, animals, birds sent out to find land — a story pattern so close to Genesis that its reading made news.

statements.s: The Gilgamesh flood story was copied from the Bible.
statements.why: The precedent is roughly a millennium older than the earliest biblical texts.

statements.s: The similarity is evidence of shared ancient Near Eastern storytelling.
statements.why: It makes Gilgamesh a document of a shared tradition as much as a Babylonian poem.

activities.anchor: his beloved Patroclus dies wearing his armour
activities.caption: place the poem's endpoint on the war's clock
activities.name: epicIliadPlace

config.prompt: The Trojan War runs ten years. The Iliad covers about three weeks of it — place where the poem's action ends on the war's clock:
config.why: Three weeks in the war's tenth year — and it stops before Troy falls; the city's fate is only foretold. The subject is announced in the first word, mēnin, "anger".

activities.anchor: Trojans are as fully human as
activities.caption: drag the divider — the frame widens
activities.name: epicFrameCompare

config.prompt: Who counts as a person in the poem — drag the divider:

before.label: Gilgamesh's frame
before.text: One friend mourned — a king's grief for Enkidu drives the plot and the poem's answer to death.

after.label: Homer's frame
after.text: Both armies mourned — Hector's farewell to Andromache, the baby frightened by his helmet's plume, is an enemy soldier given the poem's tenderest domestic scene.

config.why: That widening of the frame — who counts as a person — is one of the measurable things epics do across cultures.

activities.anchor: India's Mahabharata is the largest poem humanity has produced
activities.caption: call the size of the longest poem
activities.name: epicSizeEstimate

config.prompt: The Mahabharata is the largest poem humanity has produced. Roughly how many verses does it run?
config.why: Roughly 100,000 verses — about seven times the Iliad and Odyssey combined — traditionally attributed to Vyasa, compiled across centuries.
config.context: Its innermost layer is the Bhagavad Gita — about 700 verses inside Book 6 — ethics staged between two armies.

activities.anchor: Around these four stand the rest of the world's epic shelf
activities.caption: pair each epic with its survival channel
activities.name: epicShelfMatch

config.prompt: Each epic survives by a different channel — pair the poem with its route to us:

pairs.right: a single manuscript copied around the year 1000
creation and hero narratives transcribed secretly in the 1550s under colonial rule
still performed by griots today — the 1960 written version transcribed from Mamadou Kouyaté, who opens by declaring his lineage's authority

config.why: Manuscript, transcription, performance — the survival channel is part of what each founding narrative is.

activities.anchor: Bards did not memorise a fixed text
activities.caption: file each formula by the block it comes from
activities.name: epicFormulaBuckets

config.prompt: The oral-formulaic engine — file each ready-made piece:
buckets: theme-blocks — expand or contract as performance time demands
config.why: Repetitions are not laziness but the engine — every epithet carries metrical and thematic information, an engineering feat of memory technology.

activities.anchor: Two crafts stand between you and every epic
activities.caption: walk the pipeline from tablet to shelf
activities.name: epicCraftBranch

config.root: A broken clay tablet arrives. Walk the pipeline that ends as your set text.

start.text: Key passages of the Gilgamesh tablet are missing. What does the craft dictate?

choices.label: Invent the missing lines from the plot
Restore the gaps in square brackets, visible in the translation

invent.text: No — there is no "original" Homer either: textual criticism reconstructs the best possible text from competing manuscripts and shows its work.

choices.label: Continue to the second craft: translation

brackets.text: Square brackets — new fragments still make headlines, and scholars restore gaps you can see in the translations.

choices.label: Continue to the second craft: translation

translate.text: Translation decides what the text means: Emily Wilson's Odyssey (2017) — the first published English translation by a woman — rendered the "my name is Nobody" trick and the poem's violence in iambic pentameter, forcing thousands of small interpretive verdicts.

config.why: Read two translations of one passage and you are doing comparative literature in miniature — the choices are real.
